```ruby
class LinkPolicy
  class << self
    def external?(url)
      uri = URI.parse(url)
      return true if uri.host.nil?

      local_domains.none? { |domain| same_server?(uri, domain) }
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      true
    end

    private

    def local_domains
      [Rails.configuration.x.local_domain, Rails.configuration.x.web_domain]
    end

    def same_server?(uri, domain)
      local = URI.parse("//#{domain}")

      uri.host.casecmp?(local.host) && uri.port == (local.port || uri.default_port)
    end
  end
end
```

Choices I made that you may want to change:

- **Both configured domains count as this server.** `local_domain` and `web_domain` are both checked, since they can differ. Alternate domains are not included.
- **Port is compared exactly.** `localhost:3000` is local, `localhost:4000` is external. When the configured domain has no port, the URL's port must match the scheme's default, so `https://example.com` matches a `local_domain` of `example.com`.
- **Host-less URLs are external.** Relative paths like `/foo` return true, because they don't name this server explicitly. Unparseable URLs also return true, as you asked.

# frozen_string_literal: true

class LinkPolicy
  def self.external?(url)
    uri = Addressable::URI.parse(url.to_s)
    return true if uri.host.nil?

    local_hosts.exclude?([uri.host.downcase, uri.normalized_port])
  rescue Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
    true
  end

  def self.local_hosts
    scheme = Rails.configuration.x.use_https ? 'https' : 'http'

    [Rails.configuration.x.local_domain, Rails.configuration.x.web_domain].map do |domain|
      uri = Addressable::URI.parse("#{scheme}://#{domain}")
      [uri.host.downcase, uri.normalized_port]
    end
  end

  private_class_method :local_hosts
end
```

class LinkPolicy
  def self.external?(url)
    uri = Addressable::URI.parse(url)
    return true if uri&.host.blank?

    local = Addressable::URI.parse("//#{Rails.configuration.x.local_domain}")

    uri.normalized_host != local.normalized_host || uri.port != local.port
  rescue Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
    true
  end
end
```
